title: URL shortener
summary: Turn long URLs into short links and redirect anyone who opens one.
functional: Create a short link for a long URL, optionally with a custom alias
Redirect a short link to its long URL
Links expire after the retention period
non_functional: 99.99% availability for redirects (writes may degrade first)
Short links are not guessable in order

daily_active_users.why: A large consumer service; Bitly-scale products create links for a small fraction of users daily.

links_per_user_per_day.why: Most users only click links; one in ten creates one per day.

reads_per_write.why: Shared links are opened far more often than created; 100:1 is the usual planning ratio.

record_bytes.why: Long URL (about 100 to 200 bytes) plus key, owner, timestamps and indexes.

retention_years.why: Links printed on paper must keep working for years.

cache_hot_fraction.why: 80/20 rule: a fifth of the day's requests cover most hot links (an upper bound, since requests repeat).

server_rps.why: A key lookup served from cache needs little CPU; 20k requests/s per node is typical for a small Go or Java service.

node_storage_bytes.why: 2 TB of usable SSD per database node.
